title: Merge Intervals
statement:
Combine every group of overlapping intervals into one.

Contract
- `intervals` is non-null, unsorted, and may be empty. Each interval is `{start, end}` with
  `start <= end`; values may be any `int`, including negatives and `Integer.MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE`.
- Intervals are closed: `{1, 4}` and `{4, 5}` share the point `4`, so they merge into `{1, 5}`.
- Return a new `int[][]` sorted by start whose intervals are pairwise disjoint and cover exactly
  the same points as the input.
- Do not mutate `intervals` or the arrays inside it.

Examples
- `merge({{8, 10}, {1, 3}, {2, 6}})` returns `{{1, 6}, {8, 10}}`.
- `merge({{1, 4}, {4, 5}})` returns `{{1, 5}}`.
- `merge({{5, 6}})` returns `{{5, 6}}`.
hints: Overlaps are easy to see when the intervals are ordered. Decide what ordering makes two overlapping intervals neighbours.
Sort a copy by start. Then sweep once, keeping a current interval: if the next one starts at or before the current end, stretch the end; otherwise emit the current one and start a new one.
Compare starts with `Integer.compare`, not subtraction, which overflows on extreme values. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time for the sort and O(n) space, where n is the number of intervals.
